inline_comments.comment: `SupportedRenderer.QWIK` is missing from the `isJsx` list. Qwik uses JSX syntax (its components are `.tsx` files by convention), so it should receive `.tsx`/`.jsx` preview files just like React and Solid. The `SupportedRenderer` enum confirms `QWIK` is a supported value. Omitting it means Qwik projects will still get `preview.ts` / `preview.js` even after this change, which contradicts the stated goal of helping agents write JSX decorators without syntax errors.

The Vue, Angular, and web-components renderer snippets in this file are being changed to use `.tsx` / `.jsx` extensions, but those renderers are not in the `isJsx` list in `configure.ts` and will never generate those extensions. This creates a contradiction between the documentation and actual tool behavior. Compare with `storybook-preview-auto-docs-custom-docs-container.md` in this same PR, which correctly goes in the opposite direction (`.tsx` → `.ts`) for the same renderers. The correct change here would be to leave those renderer snippets as `.ts` / `.js`.

This line is changed to reference `.storybook/preview.tsx` specifically, but the Jest portable-stories docs apply to all renderers, not just React. Non-React users (Angular, Vue, Svelte, etc.) will have `preview.ts`. The Playwright and Vitest equivalents in this same PR are correctly updated to use `preview.*` — the Jest docs should match for consistency and correctness.

The previous text `.storybook/preview.js|ts` was updated to `.storybook/preview.ts|tsx`, but this completely drops JavaScript users. The `preview.js` and `preview.jsx` files are still valid for JS-language projects. A more accurate replacement would be `preview.*`, or at minimum `preview.js|jsx|ts|tsx`, consistent with the pattern used in many other docs changes in this PR.

The `pathExists` check now looks for `preview.tsx` for React-based frameworks. If any third-party framework package's template provides a `preview.ts` file (the old naming), `pathExists` will return false and the generator will attempt to write a new `preview.tsx` alongside the existing `preview.ts`. While no first-party templates are affected (confirmed: none provide this file), this is worth documenting in comments so third-party framework authors know their template preview files need to be renamed if they target React.

The text was changed from `preview.js|ts` to just `preview.ts`, dropping JavaScript Vue users. Vue supports both JS and TS projects. This should use `preview.ts` or `preview.*` to acknowledge both variants. Several other places in this PR correctly use `preview.*` for non-renderer-specific references.

The updated line reads: `.storybook/preview.ts is bundled into preview (TSX for React-based frameworks)`. However, for React-based frameworks the file is now `preview.tsx`, not `preview.ts`. Keeping `.ts` as the primary example while noting TSX in parentheses may confuse agents. A clearer phrasing might be: `.storybook/preview.ts[x] is bundled into preview (.tsx for React-based frameworks, .ts for others)` or simply using `preview.*`.

The 'should generate a preview with extra content' test passes `renderer: SupportedRenderer.SVELTE` but the `extraContent` contains `setCompodocJson(docJson)`, which is Angular-specific. The renderer choice seems arbitrary here (using Svelte to avoid the `.tsx` extension so it doesn't affect test expectations). This is semantically confusing. Either the renderer should match the content (e.g. `SupportedRenderer.ANGULAR`) and the test expectations updated to expect a `.ts` extension accordingly, or a comment should explain why SVELTE was chosen.

This file contains a large block of unrelated Prettier reformatting: quote style changes (`'ArgTypes'` → `"ArgTypes"`), table column width adjustments, and code block indentation changes. These cosmetic changes are mixed in with the functional preview-extension rename, making the diff significantly harder to review and bisect. These formatting changes belong in a separate commit.

general_comments.comment: There are several documentation files where the extension changes are directionally inconsistent within the same PR. For example, `storybook-preview-auto-docs-custom-docs-container.md` correctly moves Vue/Angular/web-components snippets from `.tsx` → `.ts`, while `automock-register-mock-file.md` incorrectly moves those same renderers from `.ts` → `.tsx`. A systematic audit of all changed documentation snippet files is needed to ensure that only React, Preact, React Native, Solid (and potentially Qwik) renderer-tagged snippets receive `.jsx`/`.tsx`, and all other renderers (Vue, Angular, Svelte, web-components, etc.) retain `.js`/`.ts`.

The `renderer` field in `ConfigurePreviewOptions` is now required (no `?`), which is the right design — making the JSX decision explicit rather than defaulting silently. However, the TypeScript compiler would have already caught any missed callers at compile time, so this is low risk. Just worth noting the breaking API change for any third-party code consuming this internal module.

Some documentation pages in this PR handle the ambiguity of 'old projects may have `.js`/`.ts` while new projects get `.jsx`/`.tsx`' by using pipe notation (e.g. `preview.js|jsx`), while others use the single specific new extension (`preview.jsx`). This inconsistency — even within the same renderer and CSF version — makes it harder for users to know what their own file should be named. Settling on a consistent convention (e.g., always use `preview.*` in generic prose, and renderer-specific file extensions in renderer-tagged code snippets) would improve clarity across the docs.
